profile.subseg: Male Condoms; Female Condoms; Water-based Lubricants; In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD) Kits
profile.themes: Product Diversification; International Expansion; Acquisition-Driven Growth; Regulatory Approvals

bull_bear.body: Rs.385Cr raised via preferential issue to FIIs earmarked for strategic overseas acquisition (condoms/IVD); ESOPs issued to key managerial personnel (not promoters) at Rs.140 exercise price; 50% of warrants to be redistributed to broader employee base; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: USFDA approval delayed by 1-1.5 years due to costly US-based trial requirement; South African lab breakdown causing inventory pile-up (Rs.23Cr); acquisition execution risk (timing, integration, regulatory); high inventory days (230+ days, targeting 40-45 day reduction); price sensitivity in India limiting premium condom adoption; currency and geopolitical risks in export markets
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, forward-looking, and disciplined; management emphasizes strategic intent over short-term noise; transparent about delays (South Africa, USFDA); cautious on retail spend; focused on acquisition as core growth lever; tone suggests strong internal alignment and investor communication discipline
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The Rs.385Cr fund raise is not for working capital or capex but for overseas acquisition — a strategic pivot away from pure export manufacturing to vertical integration in premium condom tech; inventory spike is not operational inefficiency but a deliberate stockpile due to export halt, not demand collapse; IVD kits are a hidden growth engine with WHO certification timeline aligning with African government tenders in 2025
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Male condoms: 89% of Q3 sales, 480M unit capacity, expanding to 780M units post-capacity; Female condoms: Q3 sales Rs.1Cr due to South African lab breakdown, backlog clearing in Q4; IVD: 8 test kits (pregnancy, malaria), CE/WHO certifications expected in 2-3 years, domestic tenders eligible from Sep 2024-May 2025; Lubricants: bundled with condoms under Cupid brand variants (strawberry, butterscotch, vanilla)

latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Q4FY24 topline: Rs.50-55Cr; female condom sales: Rs.21Cr; FY24 total revenue: ~Rs.160Cr; FY25 topline target: Rs.400Cr; EBITDA: >Rs.100Cr post-capacity expansion
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.80Cr total (Rs.50Cr male condoms; Rs.30Cr female condoms); 85-90% international, 10-15% domestic; key buyers: UNFPA, Brazilian government (Rs.23Cr tender expected), Government of India (Rs.15Cr awarded + Rs.10Cr expected), South Africa (Rs.50Cr 3-year contract)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Acquisition of overseas non-latex (polyisoprene/polyurethane) condom manufacturers in Asia to enter premium segment; expansion into US market via FDA approval (1-1.5 years away); retail distribution scaling in India (1,000+ outlets); IVD entry into African/Latin American markets post-WHO certification
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Cupid Limited is transitioning from a low-margin latex condom exporter to a diversified reproductive health player through strategic overseas acquisitions of non-latex condom manufacturing capabilities and IVD product approvals, with near-term revenue upside from backlog execution and FY25 capacity expansion. The company's path to profitability hinges on resolving South African logistics, securing USFDA approval, and converting order book into revenue.

open.item: Projecting a Q4FY24 topline of between Rs.50 and Rs.55 crores, with female condom sales expected at approximately Rs.21 crores (clearing the backlog)
Aditya's more optimistic Q4 (Jan-Apr) view: topline of Rs.60-65 crores and PAT close to Rs.15 crores as delayed female-condom sales get booked

Expecting significant new orders in Feb-March: ~Rs.50 crores from South Africa (year 3 of a 3-year contract, male+female), ~Rs.23 crores Brazil female-condom tender, ~Rs.15 crores + ~Rs.10 crores Government of India (male), and ~Rs.30 crores UNFPA for Q1FY25
Targeting to improve the cash conversion / inventory cycle by ~20%, roughly a 40-45 day reduction from the ~230-day level, by year end
Expect to end FY24 with a topline of close to Rs.140 crores
By end of calendar 2024, introduce 3 to 4 dipping lines adding ~300 million units of male condom capacity (from current 480 million units)
Company-level EBITDA margin to rise above 20% next financial year (one-time UNFPA penalty inflated other expenses this year)
Condom and lubricant business expected to deliver Rs.180 crores+ revenue in FY25
Land parcel already acquired; new lines to commence within about two years (reaffirming prior timeline)
Planning a strategic acquisition (a manufacturing setup rather than a brand, likely in Asia) to add polyisoprene and polyurethane (non-latex) condom product lines and gain faster IVD approvals

Issuing ~22 lakh warrants to six FIIs to raise ~Rs.385 crores (approx 15% dilution) earmarked for a strategic acquisition (condoms and/or IVD) outside or in India, plus small working-capital use; funds to be received within 18 months
USFDA study in South Africa progressing slowly with new questions raised; about one to one-and-a-half years away from any positive USFDA result, expected sometime in FY26
Aim to double revenue (and profitability) in the next 3 to 4 years using FY2024 as the baseline
Plan to bundle products (e.g. deodorant sprays with existing condoms) and sell under Cupid brand variants (strawberry, butterscotch, vanilla) plus Cupisure pregnancy test kits
IVD test kits: CE Mark and WHO certifications expected in 2-3 years (then international tenders); able to participate in domestic state-level tenders between September 2024 and May 2025
Working towards PAT margins above 25% and EBITDA margins above 35% as the company scales (operating margins currently low-20s)
Post capacity expansion, expecting a topline close to Rs.400 crores (not Rs.320 crores) with EBITDA upwards of Rs.100 crores
Announced a bonus share issue and a 10-to-1 share split

ESOPs issued to key managerial personnel (no promoters) at an exercise price of Rs.140 (set at Aug-2022 board meeting); existing grantees to release 50% of the issuance for redistribution to more employees
Open offer at Rs.325 per share (~26%); management will not revise the open offer price

wtt.summary: 24% guidance hit (17 chains); 2/2 projects on-time; 7 expired; 28% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and expansion-focused; management guided a strong Q4 recovery (female-condom backlog of ~Rs.21cr) and a large acquisition-led growth vision, but was deliberately vague on the acquisition target, timeline and USFDA certainty.
